COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
19.02.2024
WPMS No.1889 of 2023
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Mr. Nagesh Agarwal, Advocate for the 
petitioners.
2. Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for the 
respondents.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner would 
submit that the petitioner was bequeathed the 
property in question by the father of respondent 
no.1; that, petitioner was first impleaded in 
consolidation proceedings, however, subsequently 
on the application of the respondent no.1, he was 
deleted from the array of parties; that, the 
consolidation court has no power to delete 
necessary parties at the time of final of 
pronouncement of judgment; that, now the 
respondent no.1 wants to raise construction on the 
land in question thereby changing the nature of 
land. 
4. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent 
no.1 would submit there was no question of 
executing the Will by his father Amir Hasan in 
favour of present petitioner in the year 1926 as his 
father Amir Hasan had already expired in 1925.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner 
controverted and prayed for time to file certified 
copy of the Will duly attested by the petitioner, by 
way of affidavit before this Court along with the 
evidence, if led by the petitioner, before the lower 
courts to prove that Will.
6. Allowed.
7. List on 10.04.2024. 
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 19.02.2024
Rajni

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPMS No.1889 of 2023
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Mr. M.S. Tyagi, Senior Advocate assisted 
by Mr. Nagesh Aggarwal, Advocate for the 
petitioners.
2. Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for the 
respondents.
3. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the 
petitioners would submit that this is a matter 
arising out of the consolidation proceedings and
the petitioner has got right through the Will of 
the original owner.
4. Learned counsel for the respondents, on the 
other hand, would submit that the respondents 
are real sons of the original owner and they have 
got the Will executed by their father in their 
favour in respect of the land and the same is a 
registered Will, therefore, it could override the 
alleged later Will which is admittedly 
unregistered.
5. In considered view of this Court, this 
matter needs deliberation.
6. Admit the petition.
7. Learned counsel for the parties would 
submit that the pleadings have already been 
exchanged.
8. List for final hearing on 16.07.2024. 
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 
 10.04.2024
Rajni

during the pendency of the writ petition the 
respondents are changing the nature of the suit 
property. 
4. This Court vide order dated 10.04.2024 has 
already admitted this petition.
5. Put up on 26.11.2024, the date already 
fixed.

operation of the impugned judgments and orders 
dated 27.08.2022 and 12.06.2023 shall remain 
stayed. It is also directed that the parties shall not 
create any third party interest in the property in 
question.

application (IA No 4 of 2024) stand disposed of.
